name: MD-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Glenn Ivey running with strong fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at 98%
No competitive polling or expert ratings signal vulnerability
model.rationale: The D+39 district, an incumbent Democrat with over $450,000 on hand, and markets pricing a Democratic win near 98% all point the same way. No polls or ratings suggest any reason to move off the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or major third-party Green surge could shave the margin, but nothing in the evidence suggests a competitive race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 4th District is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+39. Incumbent Glenn Ivey is running for reelection after winning renomination, and he holds a large financial advantage, having raised about $674,000 with roughly $459,000 on hand. Republican George McDermott has reported no fundraising, and Green candidate Sam Husseini is not viewed as a significant factor.

Prediction markets give Ivey a 98% chance of winning, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. With no general-election polling available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic win in the Safe D category.
